A REVENUE PATH FOR HOUSING & PARKS

Austin City Council approved an ordinance on November 5 dedicating revenue derived from the City’s share of taxes generated by Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone No. 21 to the Housing Trust Fund and Parks Enhancement Fund.

Known as the Dog’s Head TIRZ, the zone was created in July. This latest action establishes a revenue dedication and requires annual reporting about the tax revenues.

Why it matters for housing: the City’s Housing Trust Fund supports building, preserving and subsidizing affordable and permanent supportive housing. A dedicated revenue mechanism can support that work over time.

This vote does not announce a new housing development, a fixed dollar amount already collected or a new assistance application window. Actual revenue and its use will need to be tracked through the required reporting.

For owners, buyers and renters, it’s a local funding decision worth following alongside Austin’s housing approvals and construction pipeline.

Sources: City of Austin, November 5, 2026 action notes, Item 2; Financial Services recommendation for action. The Clerk’s action notes remain preliminary until formal minutes are approved.
